subject: Crestview: international transfer orchestration, TIA scope & DPA redline cadence
messages:
From: Carol Briggs <carol.briggs@crestview.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, ops@crestview.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial scope: Crestview international transfer & DPA questions

Hi Ava (and team),

Thanks again for the demo today. Before our legal team proceeds with the DPA redline, we need to confirm how Redwood plans to satisfy the following for a subset of PII and clinical metadata that must remain within the UK/EU control plane:

- Applicable transfer mechanisms: we need clear mapping to SCCs + UK IDTA / UK Addendum (we may need both depending on processing location).
- TIA / DTIA evidence: an attestation matrix per environment (hosted vs. dedicated) and a list of artifacts you can provide (logs, retention confirmation, subprocessor attestations).
- Subprocessors: complete list of subprocessors and whether any have APAC/US routing for caching.
- Technical controls: support for customer-managed KMS/HSM, and whether the KV cache can be pinned onshore for specific tenant keys.

We want to start a scoped evidence sprint next week and would appreciate a short checklist or template from Redwood that maps artifacts to our DPA questions. Can you also confirm the timeline for DPA redline review + signing (DocuSign preferred)?

Thanks,
Carol
Principal Privacy Counsel
Crestview Therapeutics

Attachments: none
From: ava_chen@redwood.ai
To: Carol Briggs <carol.briggs@crestview.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 17:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial scope: Crestview international transfer & DPA questions

Carol — thanks for the clear list. Appreciate the priority on the UK/EU controls. Short plan below and next steps so we can align legal + tech workstreams in parallel.

1) Evidence sprint template: attached (crestview-tia-scope-template.xlsx). It maps typical items we provide (SCC mapping, PKI/KMS attestations, subprocessor list, logging exports) to the DPA/TIA questions. Please fill the left column with Crestview’s required artifacts and we’ll mark availability.

2) Subprocessors: we will share a live CSV of subprocessors and their processing locations. Short answer: most short-lived cache nodes may be in US/edge regions for latency, but we can propose an onshore-only caching path for the tenant and an affinity route to avoid cross-border caches for tagged datasets.

3) UK Addendum / SCCs: Redwood supports signing SCCs and the UK IDTA addendum. For this customer scoping we propose: SCCs + UK Addendum on the contract for EU/UK-resident records, and a TIA attestation packet that covers runtime fallback (onshore-only model variant + explicit KV pinning).

4) KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed keys via integrated KMS (bring-your-own-key). HSM-backed KMS is available on the Dedicated plan; we’ll list required configurations in the template.

5) Timeline:
- Today / EOD: share template & live subprocessor CSV (we did).
- Mon/Tue next week: 30-min call to walk the template and confirm attestation boundaries.
- Within 7 business days of call: legal redline response + DocuSign draft (target).

Next steps: can you confirm availability for a 30-min call on Mon 24 Aug (UK-friendly window)? Also let us know any absolute 'no-cross-border' flags (e.g., PII field X must never leave UK).

Best,
Ava Chen
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: crestview-tia-scope-template.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ava_chen@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 08:02:00 +01:00
Subject: RE: Initial scope: Crestview international transfer & DPA questions

Internal notes / proposed runtime controls (tech):

On Wed, 19 Aug 2026 17:08:00 -0700, ava_chen@redwood.ai wrote:
> 3) UK Addendum / SCCs: Redwood supports signing SCCs and the UK IDTA addendum. For this customer scoping we propose: SCCs + UK Addendum on the contract for EU/UK-resident records, and a TIA attestation packet that covers runtime fallback (onshore-only model variant + explicit KV pinning).

Comments:
- KV cache residency: we can implement tenant-level KV pinning to UK-only cache nodes. That requires a routing ACL and a residency tag at request ingestion. Implementation complexity: medium (needs ops change to affinity routing table).
- Batching: continuous batching currently prefers throughput-optimized pools; to enforce residency we should offer a dedicated hostpool or a residency-aware pool for the tenant. This avoids accidental multi-region batching.
- Fallbacks: plan a fallback chain (primary: UK hostpool; secondary: UK-dedicated on-prem variant; tertiary: quarantined US variant with legal guardrails) — document in the TIA as part of graceful degradation.
- Logs/evidence: we can emit token-level routing traces and per-request region tag in the audit log; will add schema to the evidence template.

Action items for legal/sales: 1) get confirmation from Kimberly that the proposed fallback chain is acceptable to Legal; 2) confirm whether customer-managed KMS satisfies Crestview’s HSM requirement or if we need a separate attestation for HSM-backed keys.

Jonas
Senior Infra PM, Redwood Inference

Attachment: none
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Carol Briggs <carol.briggs@crestview.com>
Cc: ava_chen@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial scope: Crestview international transfer & DPA questions

Carol — looping in legal with explicit redline guidance and next steps. Thanks for raising the ask. Below are the concrete positions Redwood can commit to and the items we request from Crestview to finalize the DPA/TIA packet.

Redwood commitments (high level):
- Contract: we will include SCCs and the UK IDTA/UK Addendum as part of the DPA where EU/UK processing applies.
- TIA attestation: provide a scoped packet covering routing controls, KV cache pinning evidence, per-request region tags in audit logs, and a subprocessor inventory with location mapping.
- KMS: support BYOK; Dedicated plan provides HSM-backed KMS — we will state this differentiation in the TIA.
- Evidence sprint: we will deliver a prioritized evidence list and target the first tranche (SCC mapping, subprocessor csv, audit-log schema) within five business days of your confirmation call.

Requests from Crestview (to shorten cycle):
- Provide the list of absolute no-cross-border fields (if any) as column names in the attached template.
- Confirm whether a Dedicated hostpool is on the table; if yes, we can accelerate KV pinning and HSM attestation.
- Identify the legal owner for DocuSign execution (name + email) so we can prepare the signing package.

Legal redlines (summary):
- We will accept SCCs + UK Addendum for EU/UK data; we seek to narrow the DPA Exhibit on 'fallback' to allow Redwood to route to an onshore-dedicated variant as a controlled fallback with prior notice and an audit trail.
- We propose a TIA Appendix that lists the technical evidence items (non-contractual) and an evidence-delivery timeline; the appendix is informational and does not change substantive contract liabilities.

Please confirm availability for the 30-min alignment call on Mon 24 Aug 09:00-10:00 UK time or Tue 25 Aug 14:00-15:00 UK time. Once confirmed, we’ll share a DocuSign draft and the evidence Drive folder link.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline-dpa-ava_v1.docx (document), evidence-index.csv (csv)
